summary: Wealth-management fintech Centricity raised a $33 million round led by SMBC's Asia Rising Fund, pushing its valuation to about $216 million as it expands its B2B2C wealth distribution business, private wealth arm and NRI-focused offerings.

headline: Bolt Debuts AI Distribution Engine as Embedded Insurance Financing Expands
summary: Distribution-tech insurtech Bolt rolled out what it calls the industry's first AI-powered insurance distribution platform, arriving as embedded finance products bundling insurance, credit and payments keep expanding across non-financial apps.

headline: Insurers file for a second straight year of double-digit ACA marketplace price hikes
summary: New preliminary filings across all 50 states show insurers proposing a median 15% premium increase for 2027 plans, following a roughly 20% jump in 2026, with insurers citing hospital and drug cost growth, GLP-1 spending, and continued uncertainty over expired enhanced subsidies.

headline: States race to prepare enrollees as Medicaid work-requirement deadline nears
summary: State Medicaid agencies are in a mandated outreach window through August 31 to notify expansion-population members that they must soon document 80 hours a month of work, school or other qualifying activity, with Nebraska already live and national enforcement starting for new applicants in January 2027.

headline: CVS Health refreshes its board, adding a JPMorgan data chief as a director departs
summary: CVS Health said it will add JPMorgan Chase's chief data and analytics officer, Teresa Heitsenrether, to its board this fall, shortly after another director resigned from the board without citing any disagreement with the company.

headline: Federal regulators close out settlements with all three major drug middlemen
summary: Following settlements with Express Scripts and CVS Caremark earlier in 2026, the FTC reached a proposed settlement with Optum Rx over alleged anticompetitive insulin-pricing practices, completing a sweep of the three dominant PBMs alongside new federal transparency and rebate-reform laws taking effect through 2029.

headline: India hospital stocks slide after lawmakers float room-rate price caps
summary: Shares of Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare and Fortis Healthcare fell as much as 7% after a Parliamentary Standing Committee recommended that private hospital room charges be benchmarked to prevailing three-star hotel tariffs.

headline: Private equity's buying spree of doctor practices cools sharply
summary: PitchBook data show private-equity acquisitions of physician practices on pace to roughly halve in 2026 versus 2025, down from a 2021 peak of 851 deals to about 105 in the first half of the year, as more than a dozen states tighten oversight of such transactions.

headline: Epic pushes into the AI documentation market, challenging scribe startups
summary: Epic's new AI Charting tool listens in on patient visits, drafts clinical notes and suggests orders, leveraging the EHR giant's roughly 42% share of the acute-care hospital market to compete directly with well-funded ambient-scribe startups like Abridge and Ambience.

headline: FDA advances plan to stream clinical trial data to regulators in real time
summary: The FDA is finalizing selection criteria and completing pilot site selections in August for its real-time clinical trials initiative, building on two proof-of-concept studies that already report endpoints and safety signals to the agency as they happen.

headline: Mayo Clinic's longtime president and CEO plans to depart by year-end
summary: Gianrico Farrugia, who has led Mayo Clinic as president and CEO, has said he intends to step down at the end of 2026, setting up a leadership transition at one of the country's most prominent academic health systems.

headline: NHS speeds up AI deployment to tackle waiting lists across England
summary: NHS England is accelerating rollout of AI tools including an app-based triage assistant, ambient note-taking for outpatient visits, and expanded AI-assisted chest X-ray screening now used in about half of trusts, backed by roughly £10 billion in funding over three years.

headline: Record summer A&E crowding exposes NHS hospital capacity and heat strain
summary: NHS emergency departments logged a record 2.5 million attendances in July amid back-to-back heatwaves, while nearly half of trusts reported ward temperatures above 33C, underscoring capacity and infrastructure pressure on the health service.

headline: WHO's global health funding gap widens after US pulls Gavi channel funding
summary: The Trump administration moved to cut off WHO's access to Gavi vaccine-alliance funding, deepening an agency budget shortfall now estimated near $1.9 billion of a planned $4.2 billion 2026-27 budget and adding to strain on global immunization and health-system programs.

headline: Ledgebrook Wins A- Ratings, Completes Full-Stack Carrier Build Early
summary: AM Best awarded A- financial strength ratings to Ledgebrook's two newly formed carrier entities, marking the E&S insurtech's completion of its shift to a full-stack model ahead of the 2027 timeline its founder had set out.

headline: Sapiens Taps CFO Paul Wheeler as Next CEO
summary: Core insurance software vendor Sapiens named finance chief Paul Wheeler as incoming chief executive, with outgoing interim CEO Mike Ettling staying on as executive chairman to support the transition and the company's AI push.

headline: Banyan Risk Opens New MGA Line for Digital Asset and Crypto Risk
summary: Bermuda-based insurtech Banyan Risk launched a Digital Assets & Emerging Risks product backed by QBE's Lloyd's Syndicate 1886, offering D&O, professional liability and crime coverage tailored to crypto exchanges, custodians and fintech platforms in fast-evolving markets.

headline: Indian mutual fund assets hit record ₹85.76 lakh crore on SIP boom
summary: India's mutual fund industry AUM reached ₹85,75,657 crore as of July 31, 2026, roughly a six-fold rise over a decade, driven by record monthly SIP inflows above ₹32,000 crore and mutual fund folios surpassing 27 crore.

headline: Insurers keep squeezing higher yields from reinvested portfolios in Q2 earnings
summary: AIG reported its annualized investment yield rose 30 basis points to 4.72% with new-money yields running about 60 basis points above sales and maturities, while Selective Insurance's after-tax net investment income jumped 18% year-over-year to $119 million.

headline: Allianz to buy HSBC Life Singapore in €2 billion bancassurance push
summary: Allianz agreed to acquire HSBC's Singapore composite insurer and pair the deal with a 15-year exclusive bancassurance distribution partnership with HSBC Singapore, valuing the combined arrangement near S$2.9 billion.

headline: ICICI Prudential Life moves to drop 'Prudential' as UK parent pivots to Bharti Life stake
summary: ICICI Prudential Life's board approved renaming the insurer ICICI Life Insurance and reclassifying Prudential Corporation Holdings as an investor rather than a promoter, tied to Prudential's plan to buy 75% of Bharti Life Insurance from Bharti Enterprises.

headline: Pacific Life Re strikes third asset-intensive reinsurance deal with Japan's Anshin Life
summary: Pacific Life Re completed its third block reinsurance transaction with Tokio Marine & Nichido Life's Anshin Life unit, covering in-force whole-of-life policies to help the Japanese insurer offload long-term interest rate risk.

headline: India's insurance regulator finalizes 100% foreign ownership rules and tougher enforcement powers
summary: IRDAI's board approved a reform package implementing 100% FDI under the automatic route alongside liberalized investment norms, simplified restructuring, and expanded powers to penalize insurers and fund a new policyholder protection fund.

headline: Specialty Carrier Everspan Adds Three Senior Underwriting and Operations Executives
summary: Everspan Group named a new head of reinsurance, chief underwriting officer and chief operating officer in quick succession during late July and August 2026 as part of a broader growth push in the program and specialty insurance business.

headline: Global Property Catastrophe Reinsurance Rates Post Steepest Drop Since 2014
summary: Risk-adjusted global property catastrophe reinsurance rates fell an average of 14.7% at the January 2026 renewals, the sharpest year-on-year decline since 2014, as record capital inflows and strong ILS issuance pushed the market into a buyer-favorable cycle.

headline: Auto Insurance Premiums Set to Climb in 32 States Through Year-End 2026
summary: Rising repair costs, vehicle technology expenses and severe weather claims are projected to push average auto insurance premiums higher in 32 U.S. states by the end of 2026, extending increases already seen in 27 states during the first half of the year.

headline: Acrisure Folds Tech-First Property MGA Vave Into Its Underwriting Platform
summary: Acrisure completed its acquisition of Vave, a data-driven excess-and-surplus property MGA that issues over 10,000 automated quotes daily, from Canopius Group, adding it to Acrisure Underwriting's roster of a dozen MGAs.

headline: Insurers Lean on AI-Driven Underwriting as Catastrophe Claim Severity Hits Records
summary: Conning and other analysts flagged that catastrophe losses remain the top challenge for P&C carriers in 2026, with home-insurance claim severity at record levels, pushing insurers toward AI-assisted risk modeling even as reinsurance capital eases pricing pressure.

headline: US pension buyout volume cools sharply after blockbuster 2025 finish
summary: LIMRA data show US pension risk transfer sales fell 47% year-over-year to roughly $3.8 billion in Q1 2026, with single-premium buyout sales down 57%, a pullback attributed to deal timing that front-loaded activity into late 2025.

headline: Royal London lands twin bulk annuity deals from UK charitable pension schemes
summary: The Royal Horticultural Society and Royal Society of Chemistry each secured buy-in transactions with Royal London this week, transferring the benefits of more than 700 defined-benefit scheme members combined ahead of the insurer's first individual buyout conversions later in 2026.

headline: DOL retirement-advice fiduciary rule officially vacated for a second time
summary: The Department of Labor's 2024 Retirement Security Rule defining an investment advice fiduciary was formally removed effective April 20, 2026, reverting to the 1975 five-part test, with a Trump-era replacement rule possibly coming as soon as May 2026.

headline: India's pension regulator sets goal to grow NPS subscribers more than 30-fold
summary: PFRDA chairman Sivasubramanian Ramann outlined a target to expand non-government NPS subscribers from about 9 million to 350-400 million within five years, leaning on the StAR NPS digital platform, expanded distribution, and four newly approved pension funds.

headline: Medi Assist Completes Takeover of Paramount's TPA Business in India
summary: Medi Assist Insurance TPA finished absorbing rival Paramount Health Services' licensed third-party administrator operations via a slump-sale transfer, cementing its position as India's largest TPA and unifying claims servicing across both books.

headline: Texas TPA Proficient Benefit Solutions Adds AI Layer via Elevate Tie-Up
summary: Consumer-directed benefits platform Elevate is partnering with Texas-based TPA Proficient Benefit Solutions to automate HSA, FSA and HRA administration for its employer clients, aiming to cut manual processing and speed account servicing.

headline: Old Republic Spins Off Claims Unit as Standalone Brand Lodestar
summary: After more than three decades operating inside Old Republic, the insurer's third-party administration business has been relaunched as an independent company, Lodestar Claims & Risk Services, giving the national claims provider its own market identity.

headline: Rockefeller Poaches 14-Person, $2 Billion Merrill Lynch Team in Ohio
summary: Rockefeller Capital Management's Global Family Office unit recruited Jones Wealth Partners, a Merrill Lynch team managing about $2 billion in assets led by 43-year Merrill veteran Sidney Jones, expanding Rockefeller's Ohio footprint with a new Columbus office.

headline: Vanguard Taps Vestmark to Power New Customizable Model Portfolios for RIAs
summary: Vanguard launched Vanguard Custom Model Portfolios that let advisors tailor multi-asset models to client tax and values preferences, with Vestmark selected as one of three technology partners supplying trading and tax-management infrastructure.

headline: India's Wealth Management Market Barrels Toward $287 Billion by 2030 as AI Reshapes Advice
summary: India's wealth management industry, projected to grow from about $154 billion in 2024 to nearly $287 billion by 2030, is being reshaped by fast-growing AI-driven robo-advisory platforms even as the country faces a shortage of experienced advisors for its wealthy clients.

headline: Thoma Bravo to acquire broker platform Accelerant Holdings in $4 billion-plus buyout
summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo agreed to acquire Accelerant Holdings at a 49% premium to its prior closing price, an enterprise value topping $4 billion, in one of the largest insurance distribution buyouts announced this year.

headline: Specialist MGAs plug capacity gaps as broker confidence in placing complex risks climbs
summary: Nearly four in ten brokers surveyed say their confidence in placing specialist commercial motor risks with MGAs is much higher than a year ago, as managing general agents step in to fill capacity gaps left by traditional carriers.

headline: SimplyGo and EFGH explore embedded micro-insurance partnership for gig and mobility platforms
summary: Mobility platform SimplyGo and EFGH entered a strategic partnership to explore embedded micro-insurance services, the latest example of fintech and mobility platforms bundling coverage directly into digital products.

headline: Cigna raises 2026 earnings outlook after Q2 beat driven by higher employer-plan premiums
summary: Cigna followed UnitedHealth, Elevance, Molina and Centene in posting a beat-and-raise second quarter, with stronger employer-sponsored plan profits after premium hikes prompting the insurer to lift its full-year 2026 earnings guidance.

headline: Only 7% of health systems have dedicated software to manage prior authorizations, survey finds
summary: A survey highlighted in Healthcare IT Today found just 7% of provider organizations have dedicated software for managing prior authorizations, even as AI tools like Microsoft's Dragon Copilot cut clinical documentation time by double digits at systems including Intermountain Health.

headline: Munich Re to acquire cyber insurtech At-Bay for $575 million, folding it into HSB
summary: Munich Re agreed to buy US cyber insurtech At-Bay, the largest wholesale-channel writer of cyber insurance, for $575 million, placing it within its Hartford Steam Boiler specialty subsidiary to strengthen its cyber risk and proactive-security offering.

headline: Bolt launches industry's first AI-powered insurance distribution platform spanning admitted, E&S and wholesale
summary: Insurtech Bolt introduced Connected Distribution, an AI-driven platform unifying customer data, quoting, binding and servicing workflows for agencies, brokerages and carriers across all distribution channels.

headline: Target-date fund assets climb to $5.3 trillion as income-focused series from Vanguard and Transamerica prepare to launch
summary: US target-date fund assets across mutual funds and collective investment trusts grew 11% in the first half of 2026 to $5.3 trillion, with new retirement-income-focused TDF series from Vanguard and Transamerica set to launch later this year.

headline: LIMRA holds $450 billion-plus annuity sales forecast for 2026 despite expected Fed rate cuts
summary: Despite anticipated Federal Reserve rate cuts through the rest of 2026, LIMRA is maintaining its forecast that annuity sales will stay above $450 billion, with registered index-linked annuities on pace to exceed $75 billion as the category keeps growing.

headline: IRDAI grants ProTec General Insurance its license, the fourth new insurer approved in India in 2026
summary: India's insurance regulator issued a Certificate of Registration to ProTec General Insurance, the fourth new carrier IRDAI has approved this year, comprising two general insurers, one health insurer and one reinsurer.

headline: 401(k) recordkeepers navigate fee pressure as 2026 elective deferral cap rises to $24,500
summary: Retirement plan recordkeepers are contending with declining fee revenue even as plan sponsors demand more technology and participant services, while the IRS's 2026 401(k) elective deferral limit climbed to $24,500.

headline: Edelman Financial Engines names its first retirement advisory chief to grow workplace plan services
summary: Edelman Financial Engines hired a OneTrust alum as its first dedicated retirement advisory chief, part of a broader push among RIA platforms to expand into workplace retirement plan advisory services.

headline: Corient acquires UHNW-focused $21 billion Summit Trail Advisors in its largest US deal yet
summary: Miami-based Corient agreed to acquire New York's Summit Trail Advisors, a $21 billion RIA serving ultra-high-net-worth families as an outsourced family office, marking Corient's largest US acquisition in an 18-month consolidation run.

headline: Cambridge Investment Research rolls out agentic AI that cuts account-opening from 17 minutes to seconds
summary: Broker-dealer Cambridge Investment Research deployed an agentic AI tool that automates parts of its direct account-opening workflow, compressing a process that used to take advisors roughly 17 minutes down to seconds.

headline: Gallagher's wholesale unit RPS buys Kansas MGA Med James to extend reach across six states
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's wholesale brokerage arm Risk Placement Services acquired Med James, an Overland Park, Kansas-based MGA focused on property-casualty and transportation risks, continuing a string of wholesale tuck-in deals.

headline: AI-native brokerage network American Growth Insurance makes first agency acquisition
summary: American Growth Insurance, an AI-native insurance brokerage network, acquired Baltimore-based Heller-Kowitz Insurance Advisors as its first deal in a planned build-out of operator-led agencies starting in the Mid-Atlantic.

headline: Axle raises $17.5 million to scale AI-native insurance clearinghouse
summary: Axle, which builds a programmable clearinghouse connecting insurance carriers to underlying transactions, raised a $17.5 million Series A led by Base10 Partners to expand from five to more than 50 insurance segments.

headline: Increase launches FDIC-member bank charter for fintech builders
summary: Banking infrastructure provider Increase launched an FDIC-member bank aimed at giving fintech and insurtech builders more direct, compliant access to core banking rails.

headline: CMS's 2026 Medicare Advantage rule bars retroactive denials, tightens prior-authorization timelines
summary: CMS finalized 2026 Medicare Advantage rules requiring plans to honor prior-authorization decisions, barring retroactive denial of approved services absent fraud, and setting 72-hour and seven-day response deadlines for expedited and standard requests.

headline: Cigna's Brian Evanko formally succeeds David Cordani as CEO
summary: The Cigna Group's planned leadership transition took effect, with Brian Evanko becoming CEO while David Cordani moved into the role of executive chair after leading the health insurer for more than a decade.

headline: Ascension closes $3.9 billion AmSurg deal after FTC-mandated divestitures
summary: Nonprofit health system Ascension closed its $3.9 billion acquisition of ambulatory surgery center operator AmSurg after agreeing to divest seven surgery centers to satisfy FTC competition concerns, becoming the country's third-largest ASC platform.

headline: Roche to acquire digital pathology AI firm PathAI for up to $1.05 billion
summary: Roche agreed to acquire PathAI, whose AISight platform helps pathology labs move from manual slide review to AI-augmented digital workflows, in a deal worth up to $1.05 billion including milestone payments.

headline: Massachusetts orders $8.4 million in dental insurance rebates under first-in-nation law
summary: Massachusetts became the first state to enforce dental-insurer rebates, ordering six carriers including Blue Cross Blue Shield and Guardian to return $8.4 million to policyholders after missing the state's 83% dental loss-ratio threshold.

headline: Munich Re to acquire cyber insurtech At-Bay for $575 million
summary: Munich Re agreed to acquire At-Bay, a top-10 U.S. cyber insurer with $278 million in gross written premium, in a $575 million deal expected to close in early 2027 and strengthen Munich Re's integrated cyber risk-mitigation platform.

headline: FCA fast-tracks insurtech Urban Jungle after its IKEA embedded-insurance launch
summary: The UK's FCA selected home-insurance insurtech Urban Jungle for its Scale-up Unit, the only insurtech among five firms chosen, days after Urban Jungle launched an embedded home-insurance partnership with IKEA's UK stores.

headline: American Financial Group's P&C investment income jumps 23% on alternative portfolio gains
summary: American Financial Group reported second-quarter 2026 net investment income of $221 million in its property and casualty operations, up 23% year over year, driven by stronger returns from its alternative investments including managed CLOs.

headline: Enact's net investment income rises 11% in Q2 as new-money yields top 5%
summary: Mortgage insurer Enact Holdings reported second-quarter 2026 net investment income of $73 million, an 11% increase from a year earlier, as higher portfolio book yields and new-money investment rates above 5% lifted returns.

headline: Private credit consolidation gathers pace as asset managers race to scale platforms
summary: Dealmaking among private credit managers has accelerated through 2026, with firms pursuing mergers to build scale and breadth even as skeptics raise concerns about underwriting standards across the fast-growing asset class.

headline: F&G Annuities & Life swings to $81 million Q2 loss as alternative investment income lags
summary: F&G Annuities & Life reported a second-quarter 2026 net loss of $81 million, reversing a year-earlier profit, as softer opportunistic sales margins and underperforming alternative investments weighed on adjusted earnings despite continued strong annuity demand.

headline: Brighthouse Financial's annuities segment earnings climb to $349 million in Q2
summary: Brighthouse Financial's second-quarter 2026 annuities segment adjusted earnings rose to $349 million from $332 million a year earlier, per the insurer's SEC filing, as annuity sales continue to anchor results amid a broader strategic review.

headline: LIC of India's profit jumps 24% on strong new-business premium growth
summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India's consolidated net profit rose nearly 24% to roughly Rs 13,584 crore for the quarter ended June 2026, with new-business premium up almost 7%, even as the state-run insurer proceeds with an August offer-for-sale of shares.

headline: US commercial P&C premiums post first quarterly decline in nearly nine years
summary: Average commercial property-casualty premiums fell in the first quarter of 2026, ending a 33-quarter streak of increases, as ample capital and intensifying competition push property rates down even while casualty lines keep hardening.

headline: Guy Carpenter names global property and casualty leaders in newly created roles
summary: Guy Carpenter appointed David Duffy as global property leader and Chris Ross as global casualty leader, two newly created roles meant to mobilize the reinsurance broker's best practices for clients across the property-casualty market.

headline: Aon launches $200 million 'Sidecar X' facility to streamline transactional risk insurance
summary: Aon debuted Sidecar X, a facility offering up to $200 million in dedicated capacity for representations-and-warranties and tax insurance, using pre-agreed underwriting frameworks to give clients faster placement and a 10% premium discount.

headline: Empower to acquire Milliman's retirement administration business for $340 million
summary: Empower agreed to acquire Milliman's retirement plan administration unit for $340 million, a deal expected to close in the second half of 2026 and add roughly 400 defined-benefit plans and about 790,000 plan participants to Empower's recordkeeping platform.

headline: Industry submits final comments as DOL's alternative-assets 401(k) rule nears finish line
summary: Retirement-industry groups filed final comments on the Department of Labor's proposed rule clarifying fiduciary duties for selecting alternative investments in 401(k) plans, after the public comment period drew nearly 45,000 responses ahead of its June 1 close.

headline: 401(k) recordkeeper consolidation stalls on valuation gaps and shifting business models
summary: A wave of expected recordkeeper M&A has cooled in 2026, with advisors and dealmakers pointing to mismatched valuation expectations and recordkeepers' pivot toward broader financial-wellness services as reasons deals are taking longer to close.

headline: Old Republic spins off Lodestar as independent brand for its TPA business
summary: Old Republic International launched Lodestar Claims & Risk Services as a standalone brand for its third-party administrator operations, the first time in more than 30 years the unit has operated under its own identity while keeping the same claims teams.

headline: Global insurance TPA market forecast to reach $845 billion by 2031 on AI-driven claims growth
summary: A new market report values the global insurance third-party-administrator sector at roughly $592.5 billion in 2026, projecting growth to $845.3 billion by 2031 as insurers increasingly outsource claims processing to tech-enabled TPAs.

headline: Corient buys $21 billion Summit Trail Advisors in its largest deal yet
summary: Corient, the world's largest multi-family office and non-bank wealth manager with roughly $556 billion in AUM, agreed to acquire ultra-high-net-worth-focused RIA Summit Trail Advisors, deepening its push into the wealthiest client segment.

headline: SEC forms Retail Fraud Working Group to sharpen focus on advisor and broker misconduct
summary: The SEC's Division of Enforcement launched a new Retail Fraud Working Group to coordinate the agency's response to fraud targeting individual investors, including breaches of duty by investment advisers and broker-dealers.

headline: Munich Re to acquire cyber insurtech At-Bay for $575 million
summary: Munich Re's Hartford Steam Boiler unit will absorb At-Bay, a top-10 US cyber insurer, in a deal valuing the company at roughly 2x gross written premium — a material step down from its 2021 venture valuation.

headline: Willis Re to acquire BMS Group's U.S. reinsurance division
summary: Willis Re agreed to buy BMS Re US, including its reinsurance broking and capital advisory teams, giving the WTW/Bain Capital-backed reinsurance broker an operational presence in the world's largest insurance market.

headline: Marsh McLennan Agency to acquire Iowa's Accel Holdings, expanding Midwest footprint
summary: MMA agreed to acquire the 90-year-old, employee-owned Accel Group, adding agribusiness, wealth management and retirement advisory capabilities across seven offices in Iowa, Illinois, Missouri and Kansas.

headline: AI-decisioning startup Taktile raises $110 million Series C led by Goldman Sachs
summary: Taktile, which helps banks and insurers automate underwriting, claims and other high-stakes decisions with AI, closed a $110 million round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with Balderton Capital, Index Ventures, Tiger Global and Y Combinator also participating.

headline: Providence Health Plan to shut down entirely after Medicare Advantage sale collapses
summary: The Renton, Washington-based nonprofit's roughly 440,000-member health plan will wind down after talks with an unnamed carrier to keep its Medicare Advantage book alive fell apart; coverage continues without interruption through the end of 2026.

headline: More insurers retreat from ACA marketplaces for 2027, including Medica and Elevance
summary: Medica will stop offering individual ACA marketplace plans in Iowa, Kansas and Oklahoma, while Elevance is exiting Ohio's small-group exchange, part of a wave of at least 11 insurers scaling back ACA participation amid falling enrollment and the expiration of enhanced premium tax credits.

headline: Bolt debuts what it calls an industry-first AI insurance platform
summary: Bolt launched a new AI-driven platform aimed at reshaping how insurance products are built and distributed, part of a broader wave of insurtechs racing to embed generative AI across the policy lifecycle.

headline: Insurers keep raising private credit exposure despite market jitters, survey finds
summary: More than half of insurers surveyed plan to increase private credit exposure over the next two years, according to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's 2026 Global Insurance Survey, even as investor anxiety over loan defaults and credit quality has grown.

headline: AI cuts underwriting cycle times but widens gap between insurers and disrupted agents
summary: Panelists report AI-driven underwriting platforms now pull data from electronic health records, prescription histories and wearables to render near-instant decisions, cutting underwriting and claims processing times by up to 40% — even as the same tools reshape, and in some cases threaten, the traditional agent's role.

headline: India proposes first overhaul of insurance rules in nearly 90 years
summary: The Finance Ministry released draft Insurance Rules, 2026 to replace regulations dating to 1939, adding stricter agent requirements, clearer shareholding rules and greater product-disclosure transparency; a 30-day public comment period is open.

headline: APAC insurers navigate geopolitics, catastrophe losses and AI disruption heading into 2026
summary: Industry outlooks point to double-digit new-business growth for Asia-Pacific life insurers in China, Hong Kong and Singapore, while P&C insurers in the region face rising per-claim costs tied to trade tensions and climate-driven disasters.

headline: Commercial P&C market conditions turn more favorable for buyers in midyear 2026 update
summary: Alera Group's midyear market update finds commercial insurance conditions easing for many businesses, even as RBC Capital Markets warns that softer primary property pricing and elevated catastrophe losses could pressure insurer earnings.

headline: Chubb Tempest Re names new Executive Chairman and President in reinsurance leadership shakeup
summary: Chubb elevated James Wixtead to Executive Chairman of its Tempest Re reinsurance business and named Michael O'Donnell President, effective August 1, as part of a broader realignment of Chubb's global reinsurance leadership.

headline: Retirement income tools set to move from pilot to mainstream adoption in 2026, IRIC forecasts
summary: The Institutional Retirement Income Council projects plan sponsors will shift from exploring in-plan retirement income solutions to actually rolling them out this year, alongside expanded financial wellness offerings.

headline: Outdated recordkeeping technology could be costing the U.S. retirement industry billions, study finds
summary: A new study finds legacy recordkeeping infrastructure is straining under demand for better participant tools, with consulting estimates suggesting AI-driven modernization could save the retirement and pension industry $16 billion to $20 billion in operating costs.

headline: IRDAI approves new policyholder-protection and penalty regulations at its 137th Authority meeting
summary: India's insurance regulator approved a raft of reforms — including new policyholder education and protection fund rules, a revised penalty framework, and amendments affecting third-party administrators — to align with the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act and simplify compliance.

headline: AdvisorFinder launches tool to show advisors how AI search engines portray them online
summary: AdvisorFinder Intelligence gives financial advisors a Digital Presence Report grading their search visibility, website health and online credibility, alongside a prioritized plan to improve how AI tools recommend them.

headline: Global wealth-insurance sales jump 46% over two years as high-net-worth planning needs evolve
summary: International wealth insurance sales rose from £36.4 billion to £53 billion between 2023 and 2025, a roughly 21% compound annual growth rate, as affluent clients increasingly use insurance wrappers for cross-border wealth planning.

headline: Pro Global opens a dedicated platform to help UK brokers expand into Europe
summary: Pro Global launched Pro Broker Europe GmbH, a European broker-incubation platform aimed at UK-based brokers seeking to establish and scale operations on the continent, and secured Lloyd's Europe accreditation to back its regulatory credibility.

headline: Insurance broker deal-making slows to its weakest half-year pace in a decade
summary: OPTIS Partners found that insurance agency and brokerage M&A activity fell 15% in the first half of 2026 versus a year earlier, with just 292 deals recorded, the slowest start to a year since 2016, even as private equity buyers still accounted for more than half of all acquirers.

headline: Amynta adds century-old agribusiness MGU Southern States Underwriters
summary: Amynta Group agreed to buy Southern States Underwriters, a Virginia-based agriculture-focused MGU founded in 1953, in a deal expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 with existing leadership staying on.

headline: Wildfire-focused broker RockRose Risk raises $12.5 million
summary: RockRose Risk, a US insurance brokerage specializing in wildfire-exposed properties, closed a $12.5 million Series A round co-led by Crosslink Capital and Congruent Ventures.

headline: InsuranceDekho elevates revenue chief to head its insurance distribution unit
summary: Online insurance marketplace InsuranceDekho promoted Chief Revenue Officer Abhishek Bansal to CEO of its core Insurance Business and hired Joyeeta Ghosal as Head of Marketing, as part of a broader leadership reshuffle.

headline: Payments and AI startups pull in $361 million in a single week of fintech funding
summary: Weekly fintech funding tracked by FinTech Global reached $361 million, with payments and AI-focused companies accounting for the bulk of the capital raised, continuing a summer run of steady if unspectacular deal flow.

headline: Geopolitical shocks and AI adoption are squeezing how insurers price risk
summary: Global economic and geopolitical volatility, combined with six straight years of catastrophe losses topping $100 billion, is forcing insurers to rethink commercial-line pricing models as new exposures and data sources upend established underwriting assumptions.

headline: AI-native insurance verification clearinghouse Axle quadruples prior funding total
summary: Axle, which runs an AI-native clearinghouse for insurance verification, raised $17.5 million in new funding, roughly four times its total prior fundraising, as part of a busy mid-August week of insurance and insurtech dealmaking.

headline: Costco makes first-ever move into Medicare with SCAN Health Plan partnership
summary: Costco Wholesale and nonprofit insurer SCAN Group unveiled a partnership to sell co-branded Medicare Advantage plans in two states and a Medicare supplement plan in a third, pending regulatory approval, marking the retailer's debut in the senior health plan market.

headline: Medicare Advantage member satisfaction hits new low, J.D. Power finds
summary: J.D. Power's 2026 Medicare Advantage study shows overall member satisfaction fell 12 points on its 1,000-point scale, a 41-point drop from 2024, with fewer than half of members saying they trust their plan.

headline: Employers increasingly ditch the 'Big Three' PBMs, survey shows
summary: A National Alliance of Healthcare Purchaser Coalitions survey released in mid-August found the share of employers using Express Scripts, CVS Caremark or Optum Rx dropped from 63% to 54% year over year, with smaller employers driving the exodus to upstart pharmacy benefit managers.

headline: Major insurers post stronger Q2 profits as medical cost trends ease
summary: UnitedHealth Group, Centene and other large payers reported improved second-quarter 2026 results, with UnitedHealth posting roughly $5.4 billion in profit and Centene topping $1 billion as insurers credited better cost management even as Elevance Health's benefit expense ratio worsened.

headline: Court fight over shortened ACA enrollment window heads to appeal
summary: After a judge vacated a federal rule that would have shortened the ACA open enrollment period, HHS appealed the ruling in July, with oral arguments now set for late October as the 2027 marketplace enrollment season approaches.

headline: States race to notify Medicaid enrollees ahead of new work requirements
summary: State Medicaid agencies must conduct enrollee outreach between June 30 and August 31, 2026 about incoming federal work requirements, which researchers project could cause more than 5 million people to lose coverage by 2034.

headline: AI now handles most prior authorization decisions, but debate over fairness grows
summary: Roughly 84% of US health insurers are using AI for prior authorization and claims tasks in 2026, and industry pledges have cut request volumes by about 11%, even as critics question whether automation is speeding approvals or just automating denials.

headline: Centene's finance chief to exit as insurer manages ACA turbulence
summary: Centene said its longtime CFO will step down, with a successor named to take over as the Medicaid- and ACA-focused insurer works through subsidy expiration and enrollment declines affecting the marketplace business.

headline: Singapore insurers confront surging medical inflation at industry summit
summary: AIA Singapore's inaugural Healthcare Summit in August 2026 gathered policymakers and health leaders to address affordability pressures, as medical inflation projections and concerns among Singapore residents about rising healthcare costs mount.

headline: Oracle Health rolls out upgraded AI agent for clinicians
summary: Oracle Health released enhanced Clinical AI Agent capabilities designed to help doctors prepare for visits, finish documentation faster, and improve reimbursement accuracy for health systems.

headline: Digital health funding rebounds to $7.4B in 2026 on AI wave
summary: Venture funding for digital health startups is climbing again in 2026, powered by an AI-driven rebound, with megadeals for companies like Whoop, OpenEvidence and Aidoc and AI-branded startups capturing more than half of all capital invested.

headline: Apollo Hospitals extends outpatient care to all seven days a week
summary: Apollo Hospitals launched 'Always Open, Always Here,' opening outpatient consultations, diagnostics and scheduled procedures on Sundays across its network, a move it bills as a first for Indian healthcare aimed at reducing weekday wait times.

headline: NHS A&E departments log busiest month on record amid summer heatwaves
summary: England's NHS saw roughly 2.5 million A&E attendances in July 2026, the busiest month ever recorded, alongside record ambulance call volumes, even as four-hour treatment performance improved slightly month over month.

headline: NHS opens flu jab bookings early to get ahead of winter pressures
summary: The NHS began urging eligible groups, including pregnant women and children, to pre-book flu vaccinations from August 17 for a September 1 start, moving earlier than usual after a summer of record emergency demand.

headline: ThinkSono wins first FDA clearance for AI-guided blood clot ultrasound
summary: UK-founded ThinkSono received FDA 510(k) clearance for its AI-powered ultrasound guidance software for evaluating suspected deep vein thrombosis, letting non-specialist staff capture diagnostic-quality scans after brief training, based on a 1,691-patient multicenter study.

headline: Wave of health system CEO transitions continues through 2026
summary: Large US health systems including Ascension, Community Health Network, Temple Health and PeaceHealth have installed new CEOs this year, reflecting a broader wave of executive turnover across hospital leadership in 2026.

headline: Ransomware keeps pummeling hospitals even as attacks plateau
summary: Healthcare organizations were hit by ransomware roughly 410 times in the first half of 2026, a slight rise in hospital and clinic attacks even as overall healthcare ransomware growth flattened compared with a surge in attacks on other businesses.

headline: Munich Re to buy cyber insurtech At-Bay in a $575 million deal
summary: Munich Re agreed to acquire US cyber insurtech At-Bay at an enterprise value of $575 million, folding its cyber-risk monitoring and underwriting-data platform into HSB, Munich Re Specialty's technology-focused cyber arm, with closing expected in early 2027.

headline: Thoma Bravo takes specialty insurtech Accelerant private in a deal above $4 billion
summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo signed a definitive agreement to acquire Accelerant Holdings for roughly $20.25 a share in cash, a nearly 49% premium, taking the data-driven specialty-risk exchange private in a transaction expected to close in the first half of 2027.

headline: India's insurance regulator sets up a working group to govern AI use in the sector
summary: IRDAI formed a seven-member working group on artificial intelligence with a three-month mandate to map current AI adoption among insurers and propose a framework for ethical, transparent and explainable AI use, with particular focus on claims processing and fraud detection.

headline: PGIM's assets climb to $1.49 trillion as Prudential's Q2 results beat estimates
summary: Prudential Financial's second-quarter 2026 results topped analyst expectations, helped by PGIM's asset management fee income rising on market gains and PGIM's assets under management climbing to $1.49 trillion, up from $1.43 trillion the prior quarter.

headline: RGA's investment income strengthens as new-money yields climb past 6%
summary: Reinsurance Group of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings showed new money yields of about 6.02% and variable investment income returns of roughly 15%, underscoring how persistently higher interest rates continue to lift reinsurer and insurer portfolio income.

headline: Private credit managers pivot away from direct lending as fundraising cools sharply
summary: Bloomberg reports that direct-lending fundraising has slumped -- non-traded business development company fundraising fell about 82% year over year in the second quarter -- pushing asset managers toward asset-based finance and credit-secondaries strategies instead.

headline: Delaware Life and Clear Spring probed over $17 billion in reclassified related-party investments
summary: Federal prosecutors and the SEC are examining whether the two Group 1001 insurers, controlled by Dodgers/Lakers owner Mark Walter, properly disclosed that roughly 39% of their invested assets -- about $17 billion -- were tied to Walter-affiliated companies rather than the 3% originally reported to regulators.

headline: MassMutual Ascend's advisory annuity business crosses $2 billion in lifetime sales
summary: MassMutual Ascend said its fee-based annuity lineup, distributed through more than 1,700 advisor reps at nearly 1,000 RIAs, has now generated over $2 billion in cumulative sales, with almost half of that volume coming in just the past two years.

headline: Nitrogen launches AI scoring tool to flag life, long-term-care and annuity coverage gaps
summary: Wealth-tech platform Nitrogen rolled out an 'Insurance Center' module built around a Coverage Number score that compares a client's existing life, long-term-care and annuity protection against calculated need, giving advisors a fast way to spot under- or over-insured clients.

headline: M&G completes another UK bulk annuity deal as pension buy-in demand stays strong
summary: M&G finalized an £85 million bulk purchase annuity transaction covering roughly 740 members of the Altro Pension Scheme, part of a busy year of UK buy-in activity fueled by elevated annuity pricing rates and improved defined-benefit funding levels.

headline: ManhattanLife extends its buyout streak with Union Security Life acquisition
summary: The Manhattan Life Insurance Company completed its purchase of Union Security Life Insurance Company of New York from Assurant, adding a New York life, annuity and accident-and-health block to a growth strategy built on more than 100 prior company and block acquisitions.

headline: Protective Life lines up CEO succession as Bielen prepares to retire
summary: Protective Life Corporation announced that longtime chief executive Rich Bielen will retire at the end of 2026, with current president and CFO Paul Wells named to take over as president and CEO starting January 1, 2027.

headline: BCG: softer pricing and mounting risks are resetting the US P&C market
summary: A BCG analysis found US property-casualty insurers are entering a correction phase as competitive pricing pressure and emerging risks such as AI liability and climate volatility reshape underwriting strategy heading through 2026.

headline: Global catastrophe losses ran well below trend in first half of 2026, Swiss Re says
summary: Swiss Re Institute estimated global insured natural catastrophe losses at about $42 billion for H1 2026, the lowest first-half total since 2020 and well under the long-term trend, even as underlying exposure keeps rising.

headline: nsur.ai debuts AI underwriting assistant built for P&C carriers and MGAs
summary: Startup nsur.ai announced general availability of an AI Underwriting Assistant designed to plug into insurers' and MGAs' existing systems rather than replace them, aiming to speed up property-casualty submission handling.

headline: State regulators sharpen focus on solvency, catastrophe risk and AI oversight
summary: NAIC leadership set its 2026 committee agenda around financial solvency rules, natural catastrophe resilience, and supervision of insurers' use of emerging technology including AI.

headline: Canopius pulls in HSBC operations veteran as new group COO
summary: Lloyd's insurer Canopius named Stacey Alioto, formerly HSBC's deputy group COO, as its new Group Chief Operating Officer effective September 2026, succeeding the retiring Kate Roy.

headline: UK's Pension Schemes Act 2026 becomes law, reshaping DC pensions for 20 million-plus savers
summary: The newly enacted Pension Schemes Act 2026 requires UK pension schemes to prove they deliver value for money, enables automatic consolidation of small deferred pension pots, and pushes the market toward larger, better-performing default funds -- reforms the government says could add up to £29,000 to a typical saver's pot.

headline: Ascensus to buy AmericanTCS, adding trust, custody and ERISA tech to its retirement platform
summary: Retirement services provider Ascensus agreed to acquire AmericanTCS, gaining trust, custody and ERISA technology tools -- including PensionPro and ERISApedia -- that expand its pooled employer plan and fiduciary services for recordkeepers, banks, insurers and asset managers; the deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026.

headline: Australian Retirement Trust eyes Southeast Asia for its next wave of long-term investment
summary: Executives from Australian Retirement Trust said at a Hanoi investor roundtable that Southeast Asia is becoming an increasingly attractive destination for large pension funds looking to diversify their portfolios beyond the US market.

headline: Retirement plan providers push deeper into AI for personalized participant guidance
summary: Recordkeepers and advisory firms are rolling out AI tools that combine participant data with large language models to deliver real-time, personalized retirement guidance and forecast income shortfalls, even as fiduciary oversight of these new tools becomes a bigger governance concern.

headline: CorVel's claims volumes post their biggest jump in over a year as AI tools scale
summary: CorVel reported that claims volume rose 8% year-over-year in its June quarter, the largest increase since December 2024, as the workers' comp TPA continues rolling out AI-driven summarization and reserve-prediction tools across its CareMC platform.

headline: US regulators edge closer to a formal oversight regime for third-party AI vendors
summary: At the NAIC's Summer National Meeting, the Third-Party Data and Models Working Group narrowed a proposed oversight framework to focus first on pricing and underwriting vendors, weighing whether registration should be voluntary and whether the outcome should be a model law or a bulletin.

headline: Playbook rolls out AI workflow-orchestration platform for advisory firms
summary: Formerly known as Powder, Playbook launched an AI orchestration platform that lets RIAs, family offices and wealth firms automate complex operational workflows and continuously refine them.

headline: Motilal Oswal's asset management arm tops ₹2 trillion in assets
summary: Motilal Oswal AMC said its combined mutual fund, alternatives and portfolio-management assets crossed ₹2 trillion in August 2026, helped by new product launches and steady SIP inflows through the fiscal year.

headline: Sun Life debuts global private-wealth platform to chase Asia's HNWI boom
summary: Sun Life launched a new global private wealth platform aimed at Asia's fast-growing high-net-worth population, betting on the region's expanding pool of affluent clients.

headline: FCA moves to simplify pay rules and reporting for UK investment advisers
summary: British regulators proposed replacing overlapping AIFM, UCITS and MIFIDPRU remuneration codes with one streamlined framework and floated a simpler annual return for MiFID portfolio managers, with the consultation running into late September 2026.

headline: Alliant moves to buy AI benefits platform Nava, betting on an AI-native advisory model
summary: Alliant Insurance Services agreed to acquire Nava Benefits, an AI-native employee-benefits platform whose HQ system unifies producers, service teams, HR and employees on one system, as large brokers race to bring AI engineering in-house.

headline: AI-native brokerage network AGI closes its first acquisition with Heller-Kowitz buy
summary: Atlanta-based American Growth Insurance completed its first acquisition, picking up Baltimore agency Heller-Kowitz across personal lines, commercial lines, benefits and life, a year after building and testing its AI-driven operating model.

headline: Pro Global opens a dedicated platform to help UK brokers expand across continental Europe
summary: Pro Global launched Pro Broker Europe GmbH, a new platform for UK-based brokers entering European markets, which has secured Lloyd's Europe accreditation to support cross-border market access.

headline: EPIC Insurance Brokers reshuffles senior leadership to prep for its next growth phase
summary: EPIC Insurance Brokers and Consultants announced a round of strategic leadership promotions, including elevating Adam Okun, as the firm positions its executive team for continued expansion under CEO Steve Denton.

headline: Thoma Bravo to Take Specialty Insurer Accelerant Private in $4 Billion-Plus Deal
summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo agreed to acquire specialty insurance platform Accelerant Holdings in an all-cash take-private deal valuing the company at more than $4 billion, at a 49% premium to its prior closing share price.

headline: London Broker Howden Explores Major Capital Raise Ahead of Possible IPO
summary: Howden Group is reportedly pursuing a substantial capital raise as it positions itself for a potential future public listing, continuing the London-based broker's aggressive global expansion strategy.

headline: Howden Re Recruits Senior Broker to Expand International Team
summary: Howden Re hired David Simpson to join its international broking team in London, where he is expected to help drive growth across the Nordic region and Continental Europe once he completes obligations with his current employer.

headline: New Plug-and-Play Platform Aims to Lower Barriers for Launching MGAs
summary: Exclusive Underwriting Managers launched a turnkey managing general agent platform designed to streamline the operational infrastructure needed for retail brokers, wholesale brokers and program underwriters to start new programs.

headline: Insurance Software Provider SSP Joins MGAA and Debuts AI Product Platform
summary: SSP UK and Ireland joined the Managing General Agents' Association and launched a new AI-powered product configuration platform aimed at speeding up how MGAs build and bring insurance products to market.

headline: Antares Global Launches New Scorpius MGA Platform
summary: Antares Global rolled out Scorpius, a new managing general agent platform, as part of continued investment by London market players in dedicated MGA technology infrastructure.

headline: New Lloyd's-Backed MGA Launches to Cover Ports and Terminals Risk
summary: Acies MGU launched an MGA backed by a consortium of Lloyd's of London capacity offering property, liability and operational coverage for port and terminal operators, with capacity up to $25 million.

headline: UK Regulator Raises Fees on Insurance Brokers for 2026/27
summary: The Financial Conduct Authority confirmed that UK insurance brokers will pay 1.3% more in regulatory fees for the 2026/27 financial year compared with the prior year.

headline: Number of Licensed Insurance Brokers in India Climbs 40% Over Five Years
summary: India had 751 licensed insurance brokers as of early July 2026, a 40% increase over five years, reflecting both greater insurance complexity and rising demand from buyers for professional broking guidance.

headline: AI clearinghouse startup Axle banks $17.5M Series A to expand insurance workflow automation
summary: Axle raised a $17.5 million Series A led by Base10 Partners, with Y Combinator and Cover Genius founders among backers, to grow its AI agents that automate insurance verification and policy-update workflows across more coverage segments.

headline: Wildfire-focused insurtech RockRose Risk raises $12.5M to build out risk-mitigation-plus-cover model
summary: RockRose Risk closed a $12.5 million Series A co-led by Crosslink Capital and Congruent Ventures to expand its bundled offering of wildfire mitigation services and discounted property insurance for owners in fire-prone Western states.

headline: August Equity takes a stake in niche digital MGA Starpeak
summary: UK private equity firm August Equity agreed to invest in Starpeak, a digital insurance distributor focused on niche SME and personal-lines segments, backing its next growth phase.

headline: UK regulator trims transaction-reporting obligations in broader FCA rules reset
summary: The FCA cut back the scope of transaction reporting requirements as part of a wider August 2026 regulatory reset spanning asset management, Consumer Duty, crypto and AI governance, easing compliance burdens for fintech and insurance firms.

headline: APAC insurtech investment has roughly halved since 2022 as capital turns cautious
summary: Insurtech funding across Asia-Pacific fell from about $9.1 billion to $4.1 billion between 2022 and 2025, reflecting investors' broader retreat from early-stage insurance technology bets in the region.

headline: UnitedHealth Group Posts 86.7% Medical Cost Ratio in Second-Quarter 2026 Results
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $112 billion and $8 billion in operating earnings, with a medical cost ratio of 86.7% reflecting tighter cost and pricing discipline across its benefit offerings.

headline: IRDAI Licenses Prudential-HCL Joint Venture as India's Eighth Standalone Health Insurer
summary: India's insurance regulator granted a certificate of registration to Prudential HCL Health Insurance, a 70:30 joint venture between UK-based Prudential and India's HCL Group, making it the country's eighth standalone health insurer.

headline: French Health Insurer Alan Raises €480 Million Series G Led by Prosus, Valuing Prevention-First Insurer at €5.5 Billion
summary: Paris-based health insurer Alan closed a €480 million Series G round led by Prosus, lifting its valuation to €5.5 billion after surpassing €800 million in annual recurring revenue and 1.1 million members.

headline: Australian Insurer GMHBA Recruits Superannuation Chief Jarrod Coysh as Next CEO
summary: Not-for-profit health insurer GMHBA named REI Super chief executive Jarrod Coysh as its incoming CEO, succeeding David Greig, in a cross-sector hire the board says reflects pressure on the insurer's value proposition from rising out-of-pocket costs.

headline: NHS England Fast-Tracks £10 Billion AI Rollout to Cut Waiting Times
summary: NHS England is accelerating a £10 billion, three-year AI investment spanning an AI triage tool for 200,000+ patients, ambient voice technology that generates clinical notes in real time, and Microsoft Copilot access for over 500,000 staff.

headline: UPMC-Backed Report Finds Health Systems Deploying AI Faster Than They Can Govern It
summary: A new industry report finds 93% of health systems have deployed third-party AI tools, but 63% of those are still building out governance infrastructure, with many describing their oversight policies as ad hoc rather than mature.

headline: Hartford HealthCare Scales PatientGPT AI Assistant to Reach Over One Million Patients
summary: Hartford HealthCare is inviting more than a million adult patients to use its HHC PatientGPT natural-language health assistant by year-end, in one of the largest patient-facing generative AI rollouts by a U.S. health system to date.

headline: Leica Biosystems Wins FDA Clearance for First AI-Assisted Digital Pathology Quality-Control Software
summary: Leica Biosystems received multiple FDA 510(k) clearances for its connected digital pathology portfolio, including Aperio iQC DX, the first FDA-cleared AI software for detecting tissue-preparation and staining artifacts in a clinical pathology workflow.

headline: CMS's FY2027 Inpatient Payment Proposal Pushes Hospitals Further Toward Certified EHR Technology
summary: CMS's newly released FY2027 Inpatient Prospective Payment System proposal encourages hospitals and critical access facilities to adopt and demonstrate use of certified electronic health record technology, continuing the push for deeper interoperability.

headline: Hospital Financial Performance Trails 2025 Despite Slight Gains in Margins and Expenses
summary: Kaufman Hall's latest national hospital flash data shows operating performance running behind 2025 levels even with modest recent improvement, as systems continue to grapple with rising bad debt, labor costs and a shifting government-heavy payer mix.

headline: Federated Mutual Acquires Trucking Insurtech HDVI to Expand Telematics-Based Coverage
summary: Federated Mutual Insurance acquired High Definition Vehicle Insurance (HDVI), a technology-first commercial trucking insurer that uses telematics data for underwriting, with HDVI continuing to operate as a largely autonomous subsidiary.

headline: European Insurtech Funding Tops €900 Million in First Half of 2026, UK Keeps Top Spot
summary: European insurtechs raised over €900 million in H1 2026, the strongest first-half total in recent years even as deal volume fell, with the UK leading in deal count and digital insurance brokers capturing the bulk of capital.

headline: Insurers Shift AI From Pilots to Production Across Underwriting, Claims and Fraud Detection
summary: Carriers are increasingly running live operations on AI rather than piloting it, with underwriting turnaround compressing from days to minutes and claims processing speeding up sharply as straight-through processing rates climb.

headline: InsurTech Express Elevates Nichole Gaines to CEO as Founder Steps Back to Chairman
summary: InsurTech Express promoted Chief Revenue Officer Nichole Gaines to CEO and Ron Hensel to President, with founder Ken Leibow moving into an Executive Chairman role as the company enters a new growth phase.

headline: Clearwater Analytics completes $8.4 billion take-private buyout
summary: Permira and Warburg Pincus, backed by Francisco Partners and Temasek, closed their $8.4 billion take-private acquisition of investment-data platform Clearwater Analytics, delisting its shares from the NYSE.

headline: Trian and General Catalyst finalize $52-a-share buyout of Janus Henderson
summary: After outbidding a rival offer from Victory Capital, Trian Fund Management and General Catalyst completed their take-private acquisition of Janus Henderson at $52 per share, delisting the asset manager from the NYSE.

headline: Investment managers deploying AI in the front office jump sevenfold in a year
summary: A new survey found roughly seven in ten investment managers are now actively using artificial intelligence in front-office functions, up from about one in ten a year earlier, marking a sharp acceleration from pilot projects to production use.

headline: Mercer survey finds asset managers' AI adoption real but still uneven
summary: Mercer's 2026 AI in Asset Management survey found 55% of asset managers have integrated AI into at least one investment process, 27% remain at the pilot stage, and just 18% report full integration across operations.

headline: Target-date fund investors pay up to six times more than a DIY two-ETF portfolio
summary: An analysis found that many mainstream target-date mutual funds charge fees several times higher than replicating the same glide path with a simple two-ETF stock/bond combination, renewing scrutiny of retirement-plan default fees.

headline: PwC report pegs Singapore and Hong Kong asset pools near $4.5 trillion each
summary: PwC's Asset and Wealth Management Revolution Asia-Pacific report estimates Singapore's assets under management at about $4.6 trillion and Hong Kong's at roughly $4.5 trillion, with regional client assets led by insurance and pension pools.

headline: Apollo executive points to Asia's aging population as a major investment opportunity
summary: Apollo Global Management's Eiji Ueda argued that shifting demographics and rising retirement needs across Asia are opening a substantial new opportunity for asset managers to deploy capital into the region's retirement and income markets.

headline: Asset and wealth management deal volume rises 22% as buyers stay active despite headwinds
summary: PwC's midyear 2026 outlook found first-quarter asset and wealth management deal volume climbed 22% versus the prior quarter, signaling continued buyer conviction in strategic M&A despite a choppier macro backdrop.

headline: IRDAI bars Edelweiss Life from opening new branches for six months over expense breach
summary: India's insurance regulator sanctioned Edelweiss Life Insurance for spending far above the permitted management-expense cap on non-participating business, blocking the insurer from launching any new offices for half a year.

headline: Samsung Life rolls out a digital-only lump-sum annuity with a locked-in 4.13% rate
summary: Samsung Life launched a fully digital one-time-payment annuity product that lets customers pay a single upfront premium to secure a fixed 4.13% rate for five years of retirement income.

headline: F&G Annuities & Life brings on Michael Bailey as new finance chief
summary: F&G Annuities & Life named Michael Bailey as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective August 3, part of a broader executive leadership transition disclosed to the SEC.

headline: Sun Life lines up Joseph Natale to take over as board chair from Scott Powers
summary: Sun Life Financial disclosed that Scott Powers will step down as chair after completing his term following the 2027 annual meeting, with Joseph Natale set to succeed him at the helm of the board.

headline: Resolution Re books another UK pension risk transfer deal as it expands across Europe
summary: Reinsurer Resolution Re closed a fresh UK bulk annuity transaction, continuing to build out its footprint in the region as insurers compete for pension scheme risk-transfer business.

headline: Private credit now the largest slice of life insurer bond portfolios as NAIC tightens oversight
summary: Private credit holdings have become the dominant asset class on life insurers' balance sheets, prompting the NAIC to rework its investment rulebook and disclosure requirements around these increasingly complex, illiquid assets.

headline: Employers weigh underwriters' AI fluency when picking life insurance carriers
summary: A growing share of employers and brokers are factoring an insurer's artificial-intelligence underwriting capabilities into carrier selection, as AI reshapes how life insurance risk gets assessed.

headline: Life insurers' private-credit book swells toward $2 trillion, raising systemic-risk questions
summary: Life insurers' exposure to private credit and other illiquid alternative investments continues to climb, with analysts flagging concentration and valuation concerns even as carriers defend the strategy as a source of higher yield.

headline: Fitch Warns US P&C Pricing Will Keep Softening as Competition Heats Up
summary: Fitch Ratings expects the U.S. property and casualty insurance market to soften further through 2026 as intensifying carrier competition and growing capacity pressure pricing, particularly in property lines.

headline: Consumer Trust in AI-Driven Insurance Nearly Doubles Year Over Year
summary: A new Insurity survey finds 39% of consumers now view AI use by their insurer favorably, almost double last year's figure, with trust rising when AI is applied to underwriting, claims speed and clearer customer interactions alongside human oversight.

headline: Insurers Plan AI, Storm and Cyber Risk Strategies for Second Half of 2026
summary: Carriers are shifting claims operations from AI-assisted adjuster workflows toward more autonomous, agentic AI processes for the back half of 2026, alongside continued focus on catastrophe and cyber exposure planning.

headline: State AI Insurance Rules Gain Ground as Federal Preemption Fight Looms
summary: More than half of U.S. states have now adopted the NAIC's model bulletin on AI use in insurance, even as a federal executive order raises questions about federal preemption of state insurance regulatory authority.

headline: PartnerRe Names New CEO for Its Americas P&C Business
summary: PartnerRe appointed Scott Kreuzer, a nearly 30-year reinsurance veteran most recently of Aspen Insurance Group, as CEO of its P&C Americas division, succeeding Jon Colello who moved into a president role.

headline: Willis Re Agrees to Acquire BMS Re US in Reinsurance Broking Expansion
summary: Willis Re announced plans to acquire BMS Re US, a move aimed at accelerating its geographic growth in the U.S. reinsurance broking market.

headline: IRS floats updated funding rules for traditional employer pension plans
summary: The IRS proposed changes to the calculations used for pension plan funding, updating timing and qualification rules stemming from the SECURE Act and SECURE 2.0 Act.

headline: Treasury and IRS issue standardized rollover paperwork under SECURE 2.0
summary: Treasury and the IRS released new sample forms and safe-harbor explanations to simplify direct rollovers between retirement plans, implementing a requirement from Section 324 of SECURE 2.0.

headline: UK DC schemes face a 2030 deadline to reach £25bn 'megafund' scale
summary: Under the Pension Schemes Act 2026, multi-employer defined contribution schemes running a main default arrangement must build assets to at least £25 billion by 2030 to keep qualifying for automatic-enrolment contributions, pushing the market toward consolidation.

headline: Think tank warns UK pension megafund push won't automatically boost returns
summary: A Pensions Policy Institute study concluded that consolidating UK schemes into megafunds mainly cuts costs rather than reliably delivering higher investment returns, tempering expectations around the government's DC reform agenda.

headline: Guaranteed-income target-date assets nearly double to $44 billion in a year
summary: Target-date series that embed a guaranteed lifetime-income option saw assets jump 70% to $44 billion by the end of March 2026, up from $25 billion a year earlier, as more plan sponsors add in-plan annuity features.

headline: Manulife taps Brett Marchand to lead its wealth business as Canada Retirement gets interim chief
summary: Manulife Wealth & Asset Management named Brett Marchand President and CEO of Manulife Wealth, succeeding Richard McIntyre, while Erica Hall steps in to lead the Canada Retirement business on an interim basis.

headline: Japan raises iDeCo eligibility to age 70 and eases corporate DC matching rules
summary: Japan's pension reform, taking effect in April 2026, expands iDeCo eligibility to age 70, nearly triples the monthly contribution cap, and scraps the rule capping employee matching contributions at the employer's level in corporate DC plans.

headline: Blue Ridge Associates grows ESOP administration arm by buying AmbroseAdvisors' TPA unit
summary: Blue Ridge Associates acquired the ESOP third-party administration services business of AmbroseAdvisors, broadening its retirement-plan TPA footprint.

headline: Silver and Lynx take AI-powered claims automation live for benefits TPAs
summary: Silver and Lynx moved their embedded AI claims-automation tool into production on the Lynx platform, letting TPAs auto-adjudicate FSA, DCFSA, HRA and Medicare Advantage claims by reading receipts, EOBs and other unstructured documents.

headline: Georgia shifts annual TPA license renewal deadline to August 1 under new rule
summary: Georgia's insurance regulator implemented a rule change moving third-party administrators' annual license renewal date to August 1, with licenses now running through year-end 2026.
source_name: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire

headline: AIPSO hands the CEO reins to Les Willis after Kwolek's 32-year run
summary: AIPSO, which administers residual auto insurance market plans, promoted longtime Executive Vice President Les Willis to President and CEO, succeeding Charles Kwolek as he retires after three decades with the organization.

headline: Self-funded employers head into 2026 squeezed by rising stop-loss costs and thinner TPA margins
summary: A strategic outlook on self-funded healthcare warns that rising stop-loss premiums, growing pharmacy complexity and heavier regulatory scrutiny are converging to pressure both employers and the TPAs that administer their plans in 2026.

headline: Fintech Venture Funding Rises 23% in First Half of 2026 Even as Deal Count Falls
summary: Investors poured more capital into fewer, larger fintech deals in H1 2026, with wealth management, financial infrastructure and enterprise automation among the favored categories as venture funding climbed nearly a quarter year-over-year.

headline: RIA Dealmaking on Pace for Record Year as Private-Equity Buyers Dominate
summary: RIA M&A activity is tracking toward roughly 500 deals in 2026, which would top last year's record, with private-equity-linked buyers accounting for nearly 72% of transactions including a record 95 PE-sponsored deals.

headline: Orion Advances Denali AI Platform as Wealthtech Vendors Race on AI Tools
summary: Orion is preparing to roll out its Denali AI capabilities as part of a broader wave of AI product announcements from wealth management technology vendors including Envestnet, SS&C and Boosted.ai.

headline: SEC Proposes Rule to Expand Electronic Delivery of Investor Disclosures
summary: The SEC proposed Regulation E-Delivery in July 2026, which would broaden the ability of investment advisers, broker-dealers and issuers to satisfy federal disclosure requirements through electronic delivery rather than paper mailings.

headline: Marsh, Citi Wealth and Kestra Lead a New Wave of Wealth Management Leadership Hires
summary: A fresh round of executive hires is reshaping wealth management leadership, including Marsh naming a former BlackRock veteran as its U.S. wealth management leader, Citi Wealth hiring a new investments platform experience head, and Kestra Financial naming a new wealth management chief.

headline: Retirement Industry Sees Fresh Round of Executive Moves in Mid-August
summary: PLANADVISER's latest roundup of retirement-industry personnel changes highlights a new set of appointments and departures across recordkeepers, asset managers and advisory firms for the week of August 14, 2026.

headline: India's Wealth Managers Court Ultra-Wealthy Clients as Asian Private Banking Evolves
summary: At the India Wealth Management Forum in Mumbai in early August, wealth manager 360 ONE signaled plans to capture a larger share of the country's ultra-high-net-worth market as regional banks lean further into advisory-led, AI-augmented service models.

headline: Standards body ACORD names John Kellington as chief executive
summary: ACORD appointed John Kellington, most recently EVP and CIO at Cincinnati Insurance, as its new CEO, returning him to the insurance-data-standards organization where he previously helped build its architecture.

headline: Embedded finance moves into a more predictive, AI-driven phase
summary: Analysts say embedded finance is shifting from simply placing financial products inside other platforms toward AI-driven tools that anticipate customer needs, with the global market projected to grow from about $94 billion in 2025 to over $115 billion in 2026.

headline: Health Net's move to end an assisted-living benefit leaves thousands of Medi-Cal seniors scrambling
summary: Centene's Health Net told California regulators it will eliminate a CalAIM assisted-living support benefit for roughly 3,500 Medi-Cal members by year's end, citing rising costs, a decision advocates warn could leave some elderly residents without housing options.

headline: Alignment Healthcare moves to dismiss whistleblower suit alleging it inflated earnings
summary: Alignment Healthcare filed a motion to dismiss a lawsuit from a former chief data officer who alleges the Medicare Advantage insurer misclassified $8-10 million in expenses to inflate EBITDA and boost its stock price and executive bonuses.

headline: Aon projects employer health-care costs will jump 9.5% in 2027, a fourth straight year near double digits
summary: Aon's analysis of over 1,100 U.S. employers found projected 2027 health benefit costs rising 9.5% to above $19,000 per employee, driven by rising medical utilization, chronic disease prevalence and GLP-1 drug spending, extending a multi-year run of elevated cost trends.

headline: Atrium Health-WakeMed merger draws public pushback at Raleigh hearing
summary: A public hearing on the proposed Atrium Health-WakeMed combination drew mixed reaction in Raleigh, with some speakers welcoming the deal's promised $2 billion investment and others criticizing it as a takeover of the community-owned system.

headline: Sapiens hands CEO role to CFO Paul Wheeler as it pushes AI-native software strategy
summary: Insurance software vendor Sapiens named finance chief Paul Wheeler as its next CEO, with outgoing leader Mike Ettling continuing as executive chairman to support the transition as the company builds out AI-native offerings.

headline: Ping An's first-half profit surges 36% as China's market rally lifts asset management income
summary: Ping An Insurance reported a better-than-expected 36% year-on-year rise in first-half net profit, as a rally in mainland Chinese equities boosted fee income and investment gains within its asset management business.

headline: MetLife's second-quarter profit climbs 15% as group benefits segment leads growth
summary: MetLife reported second-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of roughly $1.6 billion, up 15% year over year, with its group benefits unit posting a 25% jump in adjusted earnings on stronger underwriting and volume growth.

headline: S&P sees India's insurance sector poised for 'massive' long-term growth despite near-term headwinds
summary: S&P Global Ratings said structural reforms, low insurance penetration and a supportive regulatory environment should drive substantial long-term growth for India's insurance industry, even as slowing economic growth and profitability pressures pose near-term risks.

headline: India's general insurance industry grows 9% to reach Rs 3.36 lakh crore in FY26
summary: India's general insurance sector closed FY26 with gross direct premium income up 9% year-on-year to roughly Rs 3.36 lakh crore, with private insurers, including standalone health insurers, growing faster than public-sector peers.

headline: IRS proposes updated funding rules for single-employer pension plans
summary: The IRS issued proposed regulations updating minimum funding requirements for single-employer defined benefit pension plans, scheduled for Federal Register publication on August 20, 2026, giving plan sponsors revised guidance on funding calculations.

headline: Clear Group and ANV strike back-to-back UK broker and MGA acquisitions
summary: Clear Group agreed to buy Lloyd's wholesale broker Newman Pearce & Partners while ANV Group struck a deal to acquire Car Care Plan, a UK motor-warranty MGA, from AmTrust, in a busy week of London-market consolidation.

headline: UnitedHealth's medical cost ratio holds at 86.7% in Q2 on pricing discipline
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported an 86.7% medical cost ratio for the second quarter of 2026, aided by $860 million in favorable prior-period reserve development, as the insurer pointed to improved cost and pricing discipline.

headline: Oscar Health's medical loss ratio improves sharply to 79.2% in Q2
summary: Oscar Health's second-quarter 2026 medical loss ratio fell to 79.2% from 91.1% a year earlier, which the ACA-focused insurer attributed to disciplined pricing and $164 million of favorable reserve development.

headline: Congress's PBM reform law starts reshaping drug-pricing transparency
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 codified sweeping pharmacy benefit manager reforms, requiring semiannual disclosure of net drug spending and rebates to employer plans and phasing in bans on rebate-linked PBM compensation by 2028.

headline: India's insurers pivot toward prevention and AI-driven coverage design
summary: Indian health insurers are reorienting products around preventive care and wellness, using AI and automation to speed claims and build more personalized, digital-first coverage as medical costs climb.

headline: Oracle Health expands Clinical AI Agent with automated coding and dictation
summary: Oracle Health rolled out new Clinical AI Agent capabilities that automate professional-fee coding, enable direct-to-record dictation and expand chart-review summaries, building on tools it says have saved U.S. clinicians over 400,000 documentation hours.
